blocks.body: When a station fails, the job is to find out why. Observe, check the simple things, measure, isolate one part, then confirm. A multimeter does not do voltage, current, and resistance with the same connections. This bench will refuse an unsafe setup instead of inventing a reading.

config.intro: The supply is live. Try a voltage measurement, a resistance measurement, and a current measurement.
config.doneText: Voltage across a live supply, resistance only on an unpowered part, and current in series are three different jobs.

actions.label: Measure voltage across the supply
actions.reading: The voltmeter reads the supply. That is a voltage measurement across the source.

actions.label: Measure resistance while the supply is connected

blocks.body: An SWR meter and an RF power meter answer different questions. A dummy load lets you test the transmitter without using the antenna as the load. The readings below are the lab's cases, not a calibration certificate.

config.doneText: You kept the dummy load for the power test and the SWR meter for the antenna match.

scenes.prompt: You want to know whether the transmitter is producing RF, without radiating from the antenna.

choices.label: Use a dummy load and an RF power meter
choices.why: The dummy load stands in for the antenna. The power meter then has a proper load to measure.

choices.label: Put an ohmmeter across the live antenna connector
choices.why: Resistance is not an RF power measurement, and the circuit is not a place for a live ohms check.

scenes.prompt: You want to know whether the antenna and feed line are a poor match.

choices.label: Read SWR in the feed line with the antenna connected
choices.why: SWR is about reflected power in that path. A dummy load would hide the antenna's match.

choices.label: Turn the volume up and listen for SWR
choices.why: Volume is a receiver control. It does not measure reflected power.

blocks.body: Four stations are broken. You get the symptom only. Measure before you decide. Change one thing, the thing the evidence points at.

config.intro: OBSERVE, then check a simple thing, then measure, then isolate, then confirm.
config.doneText: Each case had one cause, and the measurement named it.

cases.symptom: The radio does not power on. The display stays dark.

evidence.label: Measure the battery voltage
evidence.reading: The battery reads 0.4 V. This radio needs a full pack.

evidence.label: Open the squelch
evidence.reading: There is no display to adjust. Squelch does not feed the radio.

evidence.label: Check the fuse
evidence.reading: The fuse is intact. The battery is the weak point so far.

conclusions.label: The supply voltage is too low
conclusions.why: The voltmeter showed a dead pack. The fuse was not the open part.

conclusions.label: Replace the antenna
conclusions.why: An antenna cannot light a dark display.

cases.symptom: You hear the repeater. It does not reply when you call.

evidence.label: Keep listening
evidence.reading: The repeater output is clear. The receiver works.

evidence.label: Check the repeater tone
evidence.reading: The tone in the radio is not the tone this repeater expects.

evidence.label: Check the squelch
evidence.reading: Squelch is open. You would not hear the output if it were shut.

conclusions.label: Set the tone this repeater uses
conclusions.why: You can hear the machine. The access tone is the setting that does not match.

conclusions.label: Replace the battery
conclusions.why: The receiver is already working. The battery is not the evidence.

cases.symptom: The SWR reading is much higher than it was yesterday.

evidence.label: Read SWR at the antenna
evidence.reading: SWR is high with the antenna connected.

evidence.label: Swap in a dummy load
evidence.reading: With the dummy load, the SWR reading falls. The transmitter can make RF into a proper load.

evidence.label: Check the unpowered cable
evidence.reading: The cable is continuous. It is not an open line.

conclusions.label: The antenna match is the fault
conclusions.why: The dummy load cleared the reading and the cable was intact. Isolate the antenna.

conclusions.label: Change several knobs and the antenna together
conclusions.why: If you change several things, you will not know which one matched the evidence.

cases.symptom: Stations that were readable this morning are much weaker. The power setting is unchanged.

evidence.label: Check the power setting
evidence.reading: The power setting matches this morning.

evidence.label: Inspect the feed line
evidence.reading: A long extra coil of poor cable was added between the radio and the antenna.

evidence.label: Open the squelch
evidence.reading: Squelch is already open. The stations are present and weak, not hidden.

conclusions.label: The added feed line is the loss
conclusions.why: Power did not change. The new cable is the part that can eat the signal.

conclusions.label: Assume an internal part failed
conclusions.why: The outside path changed. Check that before opening the radio.

blocks.prompt: Why is changing several things at once a poor troubleshooting strategy?
blocks.reference: Each case had one cause, and a measurement pointed at it. If you change the battery, the tone, the antenna, and a knob together, a station that starts working does not tell you which change mattered. You also cannot put the station back to the last known state. Observe, measure, change one thing, and confirm.
blocks.unsure: Remember the high SWR case. The dummy load separated the antenna from the radio. Two changes at once would have blurred that.

blocks.body: RADIO LAB PRACTICE. These questions are about the measurements you just chose. They are not official exam questions.

blocks.label: RADIO LAB PRACTICE
blocks.notice: Original practice about meters, faults, and one-change troubleshooting. Not official exam questions.

questions.stem: The supply is connected and you want to know its voltage. Which setup fits?
choices: A voltmeter across the supply
An ohmmeter across the live supply
An ammeter connected the same way as a voltmeter
questions.why: Voltage is measured across the source. Resistance waits until the part is unpowered. Current is a series measurement.

questions.stem: Why did the bench refuse a resistance measurement on the live supply?
choices: Resistance is measured on an unpowered, isolated part
An ohmmeter is the same instrument setup as a voltmeter
Resistance can only be measured with an SWR meter
questions.why: The tools share a case sometimes. They do not share a procedure.

questions.stem: How is current measurement different from a voltage check in this lab?
choices: Current is measured in series, as part of the path
Current is measured by listening to the speaker
Current uses the same across-the-supply connection as voltage
questions.why: The bench rejected an across-the-supply current connection and described a series measurement.

questions.stem: You want a transmitter power check without radiating. What do you substitute for the antenna?
choices: A dummy load
A higher squelch setting
A longer microphone cable
questions.why: The dummy load is the non-radiating load. Squelch and the microphone do not replace the antenna for that test.

questions.stem: A dark radio shows 0.4 V at the battery and an intact fuse. What is the cause in that case?
choices: The supply voltage is too low
The repeater tone is wrong
The antenna polarization is horizontal
questions.why: The voltage measurement named the dead supply. The fuse check ruled the fuse out.

questions.stem: You hear a repeater and it does not answer. The tone in the radio is not the one it expects. What do you change?
choices: The repeater tone
The antenna, the battery, and the tone together
The call sign
questions.why: Hearing the output shows the receiver path. One wrong setting, the tone, matches the evidence.

questions.stem: Why measure before changing several parts?
choices: So the result can be tied to one change
Because meters repair the fault by themselves
Because the first part you touch is always the cause
questions.why: The sequence is observe, check, measure, isolate, confirm. A pile of changes hides the cause.

blocks.body: Halfway through a portable outing the station goes dark. Diagnose it on the bench and restore the one failed part. Do not swap everything in the pack.

config.intro: One outing, one failure. Measure, then restore.
config.doneText: The open fuse was replaced with the correct one. The battery was left alone because it still measured fine.

cases.symptom: The portable radio was working and is now dark.

evidence.label: Measure the battery
evidence.reading: The battery still reads a normal pack voltage.

evidence.label: Check the fuse
evidence.reading: The fuse is open. The path through it is broken.

evidence.label: Inspect the antenna
evidence.reading: The antenna is still attached. A dark radio is not an antenna symptom.

conclusions.label: Replace the fuse with the correct rating
conclusions.why: The battery is fine and the fuse is open. A replacement of the right rating restores the path. Do not bypass it.

conclusions.label: Replace the battery, the antenna, and the microphone
conclusions.why: Those parts were not the open measurement. Changing them together would hide the fuse.
